questions.q: What happens when an AWS budget crosses 100% of its threshold?
options: The AWS account is automatically closed
Every resource in the account is immediately terminated
A notification fires, but nothing is automatically stopped or throttled
Billing for the account is permanently disabled
questions.explain: A budget is an alerting mechanism, not an enforcement mechanism — crossing a threshold triggers a notification while spending continues.

questions.q: What does a cost budget track, as opposed to a usage budget?
options: Spend in dollars against a target amount
A quantity of usage, such as instance-hours
Only Spot Instance interruptions
Only Reserved Instance purchases
questions.explain: A cost budget tracks dollar spend; a usage budget tracks a quantity of usage instead, such as EC2 instance-hours.

questions.q: What is the difference between an actual-spend alert threshold and a forecasted-spend alert threshold?
options: Actual tracks what's already been billed; forecasted projects the full period's total based on the pace so far
Actual-spend thresholds can only be set at 100%
Forecasted thresholds only apply to Reserved Instances
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: A forecasted-spend threshold can fire earlier in the period, warning before actual spend has crossed anything, based on projected pace.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what happens when an $800 monthly budget's 80% threshold is crossed?
options: The budget amount is automatically raised to $1,000
An email notification goes out to the configured recipients
AWS automatically stops all EC2 instances
Nothing happens until the 100% threshold is also crossed
questions.explain: Crossing 80% ($640 of the $800 budget) triggers the configured notification, giving time to investigate before the month closes.

questions.q: Besides cost and usage budgets, what other budget type does AWS Budgets support?
options: A budget type exclusively for S3 Glacier retrieval requests
Reserved Instance and Savings Plans utilization/coverage budgets
A budget type that tracks CloudWatch alarm counts
A budget type that tracks IAM policy changes
questions.explain: AWS Budgets also supports tracking how well Reserved Instances and Savings Plans are being utilized or covering actual usage.
